# Preface {.unnumbered}

Generative AI is both a technical subject and a set of decisions about how technology should be used. This book connects the mechanisms of language models with the work of designing, evaluating, and operating systems that depend on them.

The fifteen chapters progress through five Parts: foundations; system building; research, modalities, and evaluation; responsible practice; and deployment and the frontier. Technical safety, ethics, and law remain distinct topics, each with its own questions and methods.

A sustained project gives the chapters a common thread. Choose a domain and develop the design for an AI-powered research assistant. Keep the charter, model-selection memo, prompt library, architecture diagrams, evaluation plan, and responsibility reviews together as a portfolio. At the end, present a walkthrough that explains and defends your decisions. Implementation is optional; evidence and clear reasoning are essential.

Use the learning objectives to orient your reading, the terminology tables to revisit concepts, and the practice activities and discussion questions to test your understanding. Use the project milestones to connect those ideas to engineering decisions and an evaluation plan. Code and pseudocode illustrate ideas and are not automatically executed. Prompt examples, model responses, and data examples are labeled separately.

The book is an open educational resource. Readers and educators may adapt it under CC BY 4.0, with attribution and a clear record of their changes.
